title: Factor a chain map with K-flat source through a K-flat target
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the module universe [def-weil-size-convention] and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], and quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For every chain map $t:D^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ with $D^\bullet$ K-flat, there are a K-flat complex $N^\bullet$ and chain maps $u:D^\bullet\to N^\bullet$ and $c:N^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ such that $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $t$ is chain homotopic to $c\circ u$. Chain homotopic means that there are maps $h^i:D^i\to I^{i-1}$ with $t^i-(c\circ u)^i=d_I^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_D^i$ for every $i$. If every term of $D^\bullet$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then $N^\bullet$ can also be chosen with flat terms.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, lemma-factor-through-K-flat, including its final flat-terms assertion.

proof.text: The category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], since the site is small in the specified universe. In its homotopy category, [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated] gives the distinguished cone triangle $D^\bullet\xrightarrow{t}I^\bullet\xrightarrow{j}C^\bullet\xrightarrow{\delta}D^\bullet[1]$. Use the actual cone complex and chain maps, with $C=\operatorname{Cone}(t)$ and $\delta=-p$ in the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0G7D, first two sentences of proof; Derived Categories, cone convention and homotopy-category triangulated structure

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to $C^\bullet$. Obtain a chain map $m:M^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ which is a quasi-isomorphism, where $M^\bullet$ is K-flat in the acyclic-total-tensor sense and every $M^n$ is flat. Its degreewise surjectivity is not needed. Put $g=\delta\circ m:M^\bullet\to D^\bullet[1]$, an actual chain map.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, choice of the resolution of the cone; Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution

proof.text: We will use shift stability in precisely the notion [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For $s=1,-1$, the total differential in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives a chain isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes K[s])\cong\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes K)[s]$: reindex the summand $F^p\otimes K^{q+s}$ and multiply it by $(-1)^{sp}$. The two differential terms agree because this multiplier changes by $(-1)^s$ when $p$ increases by one. The shift differential is $(-1)^s d$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so its kernels and images are those in the shifted degrees. Thus $H^n(T[s])\cong H^{n+s}(T)$ by [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. For every acyclic $F$, the right side is acyclic when $K$ is K-flat; hence $K[1]$ and $K[-1]$ are K-flat.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, K-flatness of the second triangle; Definition 06YN and the total-tensor differential, expanded shift calculation

proof.text: Set $W=\operatorname{Cone}(g)$ and $N=W[-1]$. The cone formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $N^n=D^n\oplus M^n$ and $d_N^n=\begin{pmatrix}d_D^n&-g^n\\0&d_M^n\end{pmatrix}$, where $g^n:M^n\to D^{n+1}$. The cone triangle $M\xrightarrow{g}D[1]\xrightarrow{i}W\xrightarrow{-p}M[1]$ is distinguished by [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Rotating backwards twice (TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]) gives the distinguished triangle $D\xrightarrow{u=-i[-1]}N\xrightarrow{v=p[-1]}M\xrightarrow{g}D[1]$. Thus the chosen model has the required outer terms and connecting map, including their signs. By step 3, $D[1]$ is K-flat. For every acyclic $F$, the additive total tensor bifunctor identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(g))$ with the cone of the tensored map. The two outer tensor complexes are acyclic by K-flatness of $M$ and $D[1]$. The distinguished cone triangle and the triangulated subcategory of acyclic complexes therefore make this tensor cone acyclic. This proves K-flatness of $W$ directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex], using the actual tensor of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and acyclicity of [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]; step 3 then makes $N=W[-1]$ K-flat. This uses only the ringed-site total-tensor notion of K-flatness.

source.place: Tag 0G6C, proof: cone on the connecting chain map, rotated backwards twice; Tag 0G7D second triangle and Tag 07A3 cone closure

proof.text: Rotate the two triangles to start with $M\xrightarrow{g}D[1]$ and $C\xrightarrow{\delta}D[1]$. The maps $m:M\to C$ and $1:D[1]\to D[1]$ make the first square commute, since $g=\delta m$. TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], in the triangulated homotopy category [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], completes them to a morphism of the rotated triangles. Undoing the rotations gives a morphism from $(D,N,M,u,v,g)$ to $(D,I,C,t,j,\delta)$ with vertical maps $(1,c,m)$. Choose a chain map $c:N\to I$ representing the middle homotopy class; morphisms of this homotopy category are chain maps modulo homotopy. The first square says $[c][u]=[t]$. By the meaning of homotopy, there are maps $h^n:D^n\to I^{n-1}$ satisfying $t^n-c^n u^n=d_I^{n-1}h^n+h^{n+1}d_D^n$ in every degree.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, morphism of distinguished triangles; TR3 applied after rotation

proof.text: Apply the exact localization $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ of [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated] to this morphism of triangles. Both image triangles are distinguished. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q(m)$ is invertible because $m$ is a quasi-isomorphism; $Q(1)$ is the identity. Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] in the triangulated category $D(\mathcal A)$: its first and third vertical arrows are isomorphisms, hence so is $Q(c)$. For every integer $r$, the functor $H^r:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A$ takes this isomorphism to an isomorphism. The natural identification $H^r\circ Q\cong H^r$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] identifies that map with $H^r(c)$ on complexes. Thus every $H^r(c)$ is invertible, which is exactly that $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Together with steps 4 and 5 this proves all three assertions without any change of model.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, parenthetical derived-category proof; Derived Categories Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle

proof.text: If every $D^n$ is flat, the already chosen $N^n=D^n\oplus M^n$ is flat. Indeed [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $F\otimes_R(D^n\oplus M^n)\cong(F\otimes_R D^n)\oplus(F\otimes_R M^n)$: the mutually inverse maps are $x\otimes(d,m)\mapsto(x\otimes d,x\otimes m)$ and the sum of the two maps induced by the summand inclusions, first on presheaf tensors and then on their sheafifications. The two summand functors preserve short exact sequences by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]; their finite direct sum preserves them because kernels and images in a finite direct sum are computed componentwise in an abelian category. This is the exactness defining flatness of $N^n$. The complex $N$ and the chain maps $u,c$ are exactly those of steps 4-6, so their K-flatness, quasi-isomorphism and homotopy equation already proved apply to this flat-term choice.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, final assertion; explicit cone model as in Derived Categories Tag 0G6C and the definition of flatness

proof_origin.place: Tag 0G7D, lemma-factor-through-K-flat; use the explicit shifted-cone model in the proof of Derived Categories Tag 0G6C and the Tag 014A derived-category argument
